newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Stora sees brighter future for forestry.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Stora sees brighter future for forestry.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Stora painted a rosier picture of the future on Tuesday, pointing to increased volumes and improved prices.
"The total situation looks better today than maybe at any other point in the 1990s," Stora Chief Executive Lars-Ake Helgesson told a news conference after the group released six-month earnings.
"It may be that we have passed the difficult years," he said, mentioning larger volumes and price hike announcements on several products.

Stora posted a profit after financial items of 1.22 billion crowns ($151.6 million) for the first half of 1997, slightly above market expectations of 1.13 billion, and net sales of 22.02 billion crowns against 24.04 billion a year earlier.
Helgesson estimated the risk of a setback was lower than at the latest upturn 1994/1995.
"There is always a risk for a backlash but it feels as if this is a more balanced upturn than the one we had in 1994/1995," he said.

Helgesson pointed to the fact that the North American newsprint market had improved and that prices were on their way up there but refrained from saying whether European newsprint prices had bottomed out.
Stora is well positioned for an upturn in forestry trends, he said.
"It's expansion that once again is on the agenda for us thanks to the investments we have made," Helgesson said.

Stora's European pulp operations are back in the black on a monthly basis and if the announced pulp price hike goes through the entire pulp side will make a profit, Stora's economic director, Ingvar Petersson, told Reuters.

Stora posted an operating loss of 238 million crowns for its pulp operations in the first half of the year with a loss of 72 million crowns in the second quarter and a loss of 166 million in the first quarter.
